tasks.short: Watch the line for products ready to move, signal coworkers and forklift drivers, and guide the move to the right place.

steps.what: Production helper watches the line for products ready to move

Production helper signals coworkers and forklift drivers to move products: by hand signals and shouting today; after the change by hand only for close-in moves, while finding and waving down a driver is replaced by the call
Production helper checks before calling: the products are ready to move and the call is for the right station and destination
Production helper presses the call button, which lights the lamp and shows the request on the drivers' screen
Production helper guides the move and checks products reach the right place

tasks.design: A call button at each station lights a lamp and shows the request on the forklift drivers' screen ({OPS_SYSTEM}), so the helper does not have to find and wave down a driver. Watching the line and guiding the move stay with the helper.
tasks.previous_blocker: Drivers were called by hand signals and shouting across the floor.
tasks.enabler_now: Station call buttons with lamps and driver screens are simple to install.
tasks.still_hard: Close-in moves still need hand signals for safety.
tasks.human_edge: Stopping a move because someone walked into the path.

reach.learn: Whether call buttons cut waiting at stations.

evidence.claim: Station call buttons can light lamps and show requests on drivers' screens.
Systems that log who called when can monitor staff, so the works council must consent.

assumptions: Boundary: from line output to products moved; storage is outside.
Input contract: station layout set by the production supervisor; fallback is hand signals.
Watching, guiding, the check and pressing the call keep their full time. s2 keeps 70 because hand signals stay for coworkers and close-in moves, and only finding and waving down a driver goes.
Drivers' time is outside the helper's savings.
research_questions: Does waiting time at stations fall?

incremental.description: Production helper resets the call lamp after the move.

approvals.approved_version: The call for the station and its products exactly as checked by the helper in s2c, sent once to the forklift drivers' screen; a changed or cancelled move needs a new check and call.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: drivers often miss the screen, so about half of the moves still need waving down a driver and s2 keeps 85 (5.2); high: drivers answer the calls and s2 keeps 70 (10.9).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Pick products from the line, fold products and parts to the pattern, stack them for the next step and count what was folded.

steps.what: Production helper picks products from the line
Production helper folds products and product parts during processing
Production helper stacks folded products for the next step
Production helper counts folded products: marks on a tally sheet today; after the change checks the station counter against the stacks at the end of the shift and corrects misses

tasks.design: A counter at the stacking point sends the number of folded items to the production system ({OPS_SYSTEM}) per station, so no tally sheet is kept; the helper checks the counter against the stacks at the end of the shift. Picking, folding and stacking stay with the helper.
tasks.previous_blocker: Counts were kept with marks on a sheet.
tasks.enabler_now: Line counters send item counts per station.
tasks.still_hard: Folding is handwork; nothing here changes it.
tasks.human_edge: Folding a delicate part without creasing it.

reach.learn: Whether station counts replace tally sheets.

evidence.claim: Line counters can send item counts per station to production systems.
Counts tied to a person can monitor performance, so works council consent is needed; counts here are per station.

assumptions: Boundary: from line output to the output count; packing is outside.
Input contract: station counters installed by maintenance; fallback is the tally sheet.
Picking, folding and stacking keep their full time. s4 keeps 20 for checking the counter against the stacks and correcting misses; a correction is an ordinary save in the production system.

incremental.description: Production helper reports a counter that misses items.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: counters miss items on some products, so the helper still recounts about half of the stacks and s4 keeps 60 (1.8); high: counters are reliable and s4 keeps 20 (3.8).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The production helper keeps the handwork and safety on the floor; hand signals for drivers and tally sheets shrink.
role.ambitious_version: A helper who spends less time waiting for moves.
